newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint ends up vs dlr, NBH basket.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint ends up vs dlr, NBH basket.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed firmer against the dollar as the U.S. unit weakened versus the mark and domestic demand moved the forint to the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) resistance level (bid), dealers said.
The forint finished at 160.81/86 to one dollar, up from its opening of 161.02/07.
"(The forint firmed) because the dollar went down against the mark," said BNP-Dresdner Bank's Peter Sipos.
The forint closed a five-pip midday gap from the NBH bid in the afternoon.

Dealers said the forint was unlikely to move as far below the NBH bid as it did in December when low market liquidity made the forint more vulnerable to speculation and pushed it up to 100 pips from the bid.
They added that the dollar/mark influence on the forint would be stronger this year than last as on Thursday the mark replaced the Ecu in the NBH's currency basket against which the forint floats.
The basket is now made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
Easing yen futures accounted for most of the currency futures turnover of the Budapest Commodity Exchange. The dollar eased for two maturities on the BCE.
